title: Services and $http
summary: Put server calls in a factory, inject it into a controller and fill $scope from an $http response.

options: Copying code from one file into another
AngularJS giving a function the objects it asks for, by name
Loading scripts in the right order
quiz.explain: You write `function ($scope, $http)` and AngularJS supplies those objects. Your code never builds them itself, which also makes testing easier.

quiz.q: Why put `$http` calls in a service instead of the controller?
options: A service can be reused by many controllers and keeps controllers small
It is required by the browser
quiz.explain: Controllers should prepare data for one view. Shared logic such as talking to the server belongs in a service that any controller can ask for.

quiz.q: Complete the call that reads the data from a successful response.
quiz.explain: `$http.get` returns a promise. `.then` runs when the reply arrives, and the body of the reply is in `response.data`.

quiz.q: Put the lines in order to define a factory that returns an object with one method.
quiz.explain: A factory is a function that returns the object other code will use. AngularJS runs it once and hands the same object to everyone who asks.

quiz.q: The controller wants to use StudentService but crashes. Click the faulty line.
quiz.explain: A dependency must be named in the parameter list: `function ($scope, StudentService)`. Otherwise `StudentService` does not exist inside the function.

exercise.task:
Complete `app.js`.

- Add a factory named `StudentService` that receives `$http`.
- Its `getAll` method returns `$http.get('/api/students')`.
- Make `ListController` receive `StudentService`.
- Call `StudentService.getAll().then(...)` and store `response.data` in `$scope.students`.
hints: The factory returns an object. The controller names both $scope and StudentService as parameters.
Inside the controller: StudentService.getAll().then(function (response) { ... }). The data you want is response.data.

checks.name: The factory receives $http
checks.hint: Give the factory function a parameter named $http.

checks.name: ListController receives StudentService
checks.hint: Change the controller to function ($scope, StudentService).

checks.name: The controller calls getAll() and uses then
$scope.students is set from the response data
